summary.name: MacDown
summary.one_liner: MacDown is an open source Markdown editor for macOS, released under the MIT License, that was built as a successor to the Mou editor.
use_cases: Writing and previewing Markdown documents on a Mac
Editing code snippets with syntax highlighting in fenced blocks
Exporting Markdown to HTML or PDF
Replacing Mou as a Markdown editor
Installing a Markdown editor via Homebrew
summary.what_it_does: MacDown is a Markdown editor for macOS with live preview. It is heavily influenced by Mou, and its author says it mimics Mou's UI and underlying behaviour where possible, changing things only where an improvement seemed necessary. Highlights listed on the page include highly customisable Markdown rendering, syntax highlighting in fenced code blocks, and sophisticated auto-completion. The listing elsewhere mentions HTML and PDF export. Version 0.7.3 (19.9 MB) is available for download, and it can also be installed with Homebrew Cask.
notable: Built as a successor to Mou, which its author says he used daily before Mou's development stalled
Released under the MIT License and listed as open source
Syntax highlighting in fenced code blocks and sophisticated auto-completion
Installable via Homebrew Cask with brew install --cask macdown
caveats: Only macOS is named as a supported platform on the page
Feature details are on a separate Features page, not covered here
